items.title: This runtime: how ACRYL plugins are built, loaded and delivered
items.when: Always first: the layers, the plugin and package contracts, and the two delivery paths.

items.title: Verify before you say it works
items.when: Before claiming a plugin works, stating a live fiber state, or delivering a package.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.when: A plugin is PENDING, FAILED, invisible or running stale code: symptom table and where to look.

items.title: Changing how ACRYL looks: what, where, how live (all surfaces)
items.when: ANY request about colors, fonts, branding, logo, layout, look and feel or restyling: what each surface allows and what needs a rebuild.

items.title: Cordis building blocks and where each is documented
items.when: You are unsure which Cordis or harness mechanism to use: the model in ten lines and a table from what you are building to its doc and reference.

items.title: Client slots: add UI to the Web and Desktop app (panel, button, tab, dashboard)
items.when: The extension needs any UI in the app: a top-bar button, a panel, a sidebar tab, a board, a dashboard.

items.title: Tool plugins: give the agent a new capability
items.when: The feature is something the agent should be able to DO (call an API, read a source, run an action).

items.title: Services: provide a capability, consume it, optional dependencies
items.when: Plugins must share a capability, or a plugin is PENDING on a missing service.

items.title: Events: listen, emit, intercept (waterfall)
items.when: The feature reacts to, or intercepts, things that happen in the runtime.

items.title: Prompt contributions: add to the agent system prompt
items.when: The feature changes what the agent is told or how it behaves.

items.title: Skills: on-demand instructions for the agent
items.when: The feature is reusable instructions the agent loads only when needed.

items.title: Host routes: an HTTP API for a web or desktop plugin
items.when: A client UI needs a backend endpoint, or state must be shared across devices.

items.title: Terminal commands: slash commands with an overlay
items.when: The feature is a terminal (tui) command or overlay.

items.title: LLM adapters: connect a new model provider
items.when: Connect a new model provider route: the stream protocol and a working network-free adapter.

items.title: Packaging a plugin, and generated capabilities
items.when: Writing package.json and the patch, sharing the plugin, or recording a generated capability's permissions and provenance.

items.title: Three-role capability: definition, providers, consumers
items.when: Several interchangeable implementations of one capability that consumers must not care about; swapping providers.

items.title: Profile and install services (desktopProfiles, desktopPnpm, livePluginActivation)
items.when: A plugin needs the active profile, package operations or live activation of another plugin.

items.title: Agent presets and personas
items.when: A different session composition (tools, prompt, skills) or identity, such as a reviewer or a minimal agent.

items.title: Chat slash commands
items.when: A /command the user types in the chat that runs on the host without the model (reload, export, toggle).

items.title: Theme, colors and fonts (Web and Desktop client theme service)
items.when: Change colors, surfaces, accent, fonts or text size of the Web or Desktop app: overrideTokens, register, setFontSize.

items.title: Branding: logo, name, tab title, favicon, page shell
items.when: Rebrand the app: brand slots, the tab or window title, favicon, page background, and what is native or compiled-in.

items.title: The Desktop (Electron) app: structure and what a plugin can or cannot change
items.when: Any Desktop request: main process versus renderer, modes, files for window chrome, icon, menu, tray, and what needs a rebuild.

items.title: The terminal UI: pi-tui components, theming, branding
items.when: Build or restyle terminal UI: the Component contract, built-in components, palette, width safety, and what is compiled into the CLI.

items.title: Deliver a plugin live: local install, no restart
items.when: The plugin is written and must become live now; a plugin must be CHANGED, FIXED, IMPROVED or REMOVED; acryl_install_plugin returned an error; or the plugin is PENDING, FAILED or not visible.

items.title: Delivering through the marketplace
items.when: The user wants to share or publish a plugin: readiness checks and the human publish step.

items.title: Mount points per surface: where UI and host extensions attach (CLI, Web, Desktop)
items.when: You must decide WHERE something mounts: which slot, terminal overlay, host service or Desktop frame, and which surface supports it.

items.title: Theme tokens: every design token you can override (Web and Desktop)
items.when: You want to change colors, surfaces, borders, buttons or fonts of the Web or Desktop app: the exact token names with light and dark values.

items.title: Plugin taxonomy: every plugin type and every shipped plugin, per surface
items.when: You want the full list of plugin types, which surfaces have them, whether an agent can author one, and real shipped plugins to study.

examples.teaches: The smallest plugin: named exports name and apply, no dependencies.
A Service subclass provides a named service; export the class as apply.
inject is a hard dependency (PENDING then ACTIVE); ctx.get is optional.
Register a model-callable tool with defineTool.
Listen to and emit an event; waterfall must call next().
A Schemastery Config validated before apply.
Add a static section to the system prompt.
Provide a bundled skill (name and description in context, body on demand).
Serve an HTTP route from a web or desktop host plugin.
A UI plugin with no build step: top-bar button and panel, hand-written client bundle.
A slash command with an overlay in the terminal UI.
The shape of a publishable, reviewable generated capability.
A host plugin whose code hot-updates: a never-changing shim re-imports impl.js with a cache-busting query.
the LlmAdapter stream protocol and registerAdapter, with no network.
provider A of a named capability (Service subclass); definition is the name plus method shape.
provider B: swap it for A and the consumer keeps working.
a consumer that depends on the service name only; PENDING until a provider exists, remounts on swap.
reading desktopProfiles portably: current everywhere, list only on Desktop.
an agent preset directory: agent.cordis.yml plus preset.yml, a persona-only reviewer.
a right-sidebar tab in two stages (tab type, then body) with no build step.
a /command handled on the host without the model, via ctx.commands.register.
a validated settings section with installSection, setSource and onChange.
restyle colors and font with ctx.theme.overrideTokens (both modes) and keep a custom tab title with an observer.
brand the served page from the host: favicon and CSS via webserver/index-inject rows, title via tapIndex (pre-boot only).
a themed pi-tui overlay: Container, Text, SelectList, a semantic palette, and width-safe rendering.
